nodes.label: bootcamp-deck skill (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Entry skill for EVERY touch to a slide (new, one-line fix, restyle, reorder, delete); the description deliberately says no edit is too small to invoke it for.

nodes.label: Self-contained offline RTL slide deck
nodes.rationale: project-package/slides/day-NN.html: no build step, no framework; plain HTML sections, one shared stylesheet, one shared script. Offline because the training room may have no wifi.

nodes.label: Trainees read only the slides
nodes.rationale: Slides ship inside the trainee package next to PRODUCT.md; CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and the curriculum are addressed to Claude. So any trainee-facing content must be on a slide, complete, with no 'see section N of the guide' dependency (CLAUDE.md A.6.1).

nodes.label: project-package (trainee package)
nodes.rationale: Contains slides/, PRODUCT.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and the curriculum; only slides and PRODUCT.md are read by a person.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md (trainee answers file)
nodes.rationale: The only trainee-written file; holds the trainee's own answers, shipped alongside the slides.

nodes.label: Project CLAUDE.md (A.5/A.6 standards)
nodes.rationale: Project memory holding the deck standards A.6.1-A.6.13 and the trainee-example discipline A.5 that this skill operationalises.

nodes.label: Any edit counts: read skill first
nodes.rationale: Fixing one command's styling, inserting a missed step or rewording a sentence on a shipped slide goes through the whole skill. Read it before the edit, not after a review catches what it would have caught.

nodes.label: Incident: chrome-devtools slide used tok-code
nodes.rationale: A slide edited without reading the skill shipped with commands AND output both wrapped in a plain tok-code span instead of the .snipbox / bare .snip components.

nodes.label: Reference files to read before touching a slide
nodes.rationale: deck-anatomy.md always; day-deck-recipe.md when building days 2-10; showcase-strategy.md when deciding what fills the explain session; archived plan only for historical why.

nodes.label: archived-plan-2026-09-08.md
nodes.rationale: Unvetted dump with known errors, flagged in its own header; read only for historical why.

nodes.label: Day 1 cost 47 turns: copy, never re-invent
nodes.rationale: Biggest time sink is re-inventing a component that exists. Before writing markup find it in deck-anatomy.md and copy the real thing.

nodes.label: Five things reviews actually fail on
nodes.rationale: Intro says 'hold these four in mind' but five numbered items follow (overflow guard, scaled-unit trap, growing not splitting, commands/output components, stepvid timestamps).

nodes.label: Overflow guard is the gate
nodes.rationale: Slide frames are overflow:hidden so excess content is silently clipped and the presenter finds out in the room. deck.js measures every slide; nothing is done until deckAudit prints 'N slides, none overflow'.

nodes.label: Guard measures border boxes, skips inline
nodes.rationale: Cairo's glyph box is taller than its em, so scrollHeight > clientHeight fires on any heading even when nothing is clipped (ink bleed). No amount of splitting clears it. Do not 'fix' the guard to use scrollHeight.

nodes.label: Guard cannot see too-empty slides
nodes.rationale: Incident (Day 5): two slides, a bare .flow ordered list and a two-card row, were legal and deckAudit-clean yet used under a third of the frame. Density is invisible to the guard; screenshot every new slide and judge by eye (CLAUDE.md A.6.12).

nodes.label: Scaled-unit trap (divide by --deck-scale)
nodes.rationale: The 1920x1080 frame is transform:scale(--deck-scale): getBoundingClientRect returns scaled device px while getComputedStyle().lineHeight returns unscaled CSS px. Comparing directly once produced a confident '0 wrapped task labels' that one screenshot disproved.

nodes.label: Growing a slide is not splitting it
nodes.rationale: Slide count is a budget. Self-contained means richer cards, a real example, a flow line inside the existing frame; splitting into 1/2 + 2/2 is a last resort and adding a slide is a deliberate requested change (CLAUDE.md A.6.2).

nodes.label: Overflow fixes that have worked
nodes.rationale: Fold an instruction line into a card title; convert a lead paragraph to a compact callout; tighten a gap from --sp-3 to --sp-2; reclaim dead space with align-content: safe center. The 'safe' keyword is load-bearing: plain center overflows both ways, pushing content out through the top where trimming below can never recover it.

nodes.label: Commands and output ride fixed components
nodes.rationale: A trainee must paste a command and recognise output; an inline tok-code span serves neither and gives no copy affordance. Typed/pasted string = full .snipbox with copy button; output = bare .snip without wrapper or button. After any command/output edit grep the slide for tok-code and confirm every hit is a passing mention.

nodes.label: Test: does the step ask to reproduce it
nodes.rationale: Not length or how code-like: a single bare word the trainee must find inside a longer list (claude-plugins-official) is still output and gets the bare .snip. Reserve inline tok-code for a short passing mention of a name.

nodes.label: Conditional action gets its own step--new row
nodes.rationale: An 'if it isn't listed, add it' branch the recording does not show still gets a full stepvid__step--new row (amber 'مضافة' mark, no data-t) in its correct sequence position, never a parenthetical in the neighbouring step. An omitted data-t is enough for initStepVideos to skip it.

nodes.label: stepvid timestamps are claims: verify each frame
nodes.rationale: A data-t value asserts 'at this second the recording shows this'; it is true or not, never estimated. Went wrong three times in different ways. Common failure mode: a low-resolution, widely spaced sample (contact sheet, transcript, memory) stands in for the actual frame.

nodes.label: Incident: deployment.mp4 steps from transcript
nodes.rationale: An early pass built the step list from a transcript instead of the video itself.

nodes.label: Incident: slide 9 timing 'completely wrong'
nodes.rationale: tasks-10.3-11.1-11.2.mp4: a pass sampled the video on a fixed 8-second grid and eyeballed thumbnails to place steps. User: 'Your timing is completely wrong!!'. Rebuilt against frames extracted at the user's own corrected timestamps.

nodes.label: Incident: slide 13 seeked PTS labels wrong
nodes.rationale: tasks_12.1_12.2.mp4: sheets built with ffmpeg -ss looked internally consistent and were read with confidence, but the burned-in drawtext times were offset from true time by a drifting amount. Caught only by a deliberate showinfo cross-check.

nodes.label: ffmpeg -ss silently resets PTS to ~0
nodes.rationale: On this file ffmpeg -ss (before or after -i) resets decoded frames' PTS to ~0 (showinfo pts_time:0 for every non-zero offset). A constant drift looks exactly as consistent as the truth, so a label that looks consistent across a sheet is not evidence.

nodes.label: Use trim=start=X:end=Y instead of -ss
nodes.rationale: trim operates on the normal decoded stream with no seek discontinuity so PTS stay true (verified: trim=start=188:end=192 reported pts_time 188, 188.03...). Never trust a seeked timestamp label without a showinfo or trim cross-check.

nodes.label: Incident: blurry thumbnail misread as wrong-password test
nodes.rationale: Building task-7.11.mp4's step list, a contact-sheet cell looked like a 'test the login with a wrong password' prompt, contradicting the skill's own never-type-a-password rule. A full-resolution frame showed something else entirely; caught only because the check happened before the step was written.

nodes.label: Two passes: coarse sheet, then full frame
nodes.rationale: (1) Coarse pass: contact sheet (tile=NxN at fps=1/N) to find rough shape and approximate seconds. (2) Verification pass: for every timestamp written into data-t, extract that second as a full-resolution single frame (ffmpeg -ss <t> -frames:v 1) and read it before typing the step title. Never promote a coarse guess straight into data-t.

nodes.label: Writing the Arabic (register rules)
nodes.rationale: Hub for the trainee-facing register rules: pitch level, plain spoken tone, vocabulary, bidi, numerals, و-glue.

nodes.label: Pitch to heard-of-but-unknown level
nodes.rationale: The trainee has heard backend, frontend, server, hosting but not how they work. Give what it is, what it does, when you'd use it, then stop; depth beyond that is Claude's job and costs comprehension on a slide (A.6.4).

nodes.label: Plain, spoken, never compressed
nodes.rationale: Write it the way you'd say it aloud, short sentences. Telegraphic phrasing where each word carries a paragraph reads as obfuscated, not concise; canonical bad example «تطبيق، فعملك، فمراجعة» (A.6.3).

nodes.label: A rule must name its applying test
nodes.rationale: Never compressed is not only register: slide 11's addition rule «إن خدم شاشة موجودة فأضِفه قسمًا لها…» never said how to tell if something 'serves' an existing screen; the missing test was: does it open at its own URL or just add to an existing screen? Read a sentence back and ask 'could I apply this to a new case right now' (A.6.13).

nodes.label: Never heavily dialectal (المحكية البيضاء)
nodes.rationale: The other edge, which reviews keep catching: lean colloquial but use spoken words any Arabic reader parses, not Gulf-only. يقدّم/يعمل/ينفّذ not يسوّي; ايش not وش; يحتاج/يبي not يبغى; «كل ما احتجت» not «وقت ما التبس». Colloquial connectives (اللي، عشان، بس، مو) stay; dialect verbs shut non-Gulf readers out.

nodes.label: Never open a row or title with a و-word
nodes.rationale: Includes «وايش» and «ووين»; they read as a fragment continuing something that isn't there. Mid-sentence the same words are fine.

nodes.label: One trainee, singular, always
nodes.rationale: Each trainee builds alone. A plural reads as 'me and the other trainees' or 'me and Claude', and Claude is a tool the trainee operates. Never «تشتغلون/وصلتم/توصلون/أنتم/سوا» with Claude as the other party; say «في كل مهمّة عليك شغل، وعلى Claude شغل». Exception: trainer plus room in a live session («ننجزها معًا الآن», §7.10). (A.6.7.1)

nodes.label: Concrete examples only
nodes.rationale: «لو عندك متجر وتبغى تعرف كم طلب وصلك اليوم» beats «مثال على استعلام البيانات». If an example can't be made concrete it isn't understood well enough to teach (A.6.5).

nodes.label: Example assuming unestablished domain is borrowed scenery
nodes.rationale: Incident: a Day-2 slide explained role overlap with «مقدّم الخدمة حجز مواعيده الخاصّة», vivid only if you already hold a booking domain the deck never set up. Test: could a trainee who read only this deck, to this slide, picture it? Prefer the example that day's own recording is about to play: no setup cost, pays twice.

nodes.label: Calibrate how much rides on the example
nodes.rationale: Examples beat abstraction but the dose is a judgement. Test: could the trainee understand the definition cold? Then clarifying; if the definition would land as noise first, gateway. Most topics do not clear the gateway bar; over-dosing a light topic buys nothing (CLAUDE.md A.6.11).

nodes.label: Clarifying example (default dose)
nodes.rationale: One line, one card, a real number, inside the explanation.

nodes.label: Gateway example (rare, deliberate)
nodes.rationale: For heavy/technical topics: open on a situation the trainee already lives, walk it as a sequence, never name the concept while the story runs, reveal in the closing line, then explain on the next slide by pointing back at it. Earns a whole slide.

nodes.label: §7.5 MCP: the worked gateway case
nodes.rationale: Slide 24 is the Gmail story with MCP unnamed until its last line; slide 25 names the parts by reflecting them back onto it. A gateway's badge and title can spoil its own reveal, so slide 24's badge had to change too.

nodes.label: Show the flow before the work
nodes.rationale: Never drop trainees into steps without saying plainly what the sequence is for and in what order. Medium-neutral: some framings belong on a slide, others are just something the trainer says; decide per case and say which (A.6.6).

nodes.label: Verb person matters (ن- vs ت-)
nodes.rationale: «ن-» verbs mean we do this together: right for «تطبيق مع المدرب», wrong for «مراجعة وعرض التقدم» and for anything the trainee does alone. Incident: «نجهّز جهازك» when the trainer only demonstrates promises something the session does not keep.

nodes.label: Fixed vocabulary table
nodes.rationale: Hub for the choices that never vary on trainee-facing text (CLAUDE.md A.6.7).

nodes.label: مشروع not منتج
nodes.rationale: Trainees build projects, not products.

nodes.label: الدورة / القسم N / الحزمة, never دليل
nodes.rationale: The deck is the curriculum; there is no separate guide.

nodes.label: منهج means curriculum (not محتوى)
nodes.rationale: Use منهج where curriculum is meant, never محتوى.

nodes.label: محتوى الملفات / فهرس المحتويات, never منهج
nodes.rationale: These are file contents and a table of contents.

nodes.label: ايش, never وش/ويش/ووش
nodes.rationale: The colloquial 'what' is ايش; the و is a separate conjunction, not part of it. وايش is wrong as the default.

nodes.label: يقدّم/يعمل/ينفّذ, never يسوّي
nodes.rationale: Gulf-only verb; the register stays spoken without it.

nodes.label: سطر الأوامر / موجّه الأوامر, never الطرفية
nodes.rationale: سطر الأوامر for the concept, موجّه الأوامر for a window you open, Terminal/PowerShell for a named program. الطرفية reads as stilted; hand-corrected out of the deck repeatedly before the rule was written down.

nodes.label: مجموعة شرائح, never بلوك
nodes.rationale: No English words spelled in Arabic letters.

nodes.label: ملفات تشغيل الشرائح, never ما يخصّك
nodes.rationale: Never phrase something as beneath the trainee.

nodes.label: خصائص, never مجالات/نقاط/عناصر نطاق
nodes.rationale: The scope list is خصائص derived from غايات; the terminology box bans every synonym.

nodes.label: مشروع الأولي (except MVP phrase)
nodes.rationale: منتج survives only as the P in «المنتج التقني الأولي (MVP)» and in the programme's own name.

nodes.label: ربط until §7.5 defines التكامل
nodes.rationale: Never التكاملات before slide 23; ربط is plainer and the noun is not introduced yet.

nodes.label: موعد / مواعيد متاحة, never التوفّر
nodes.rationale: Use موعد, مواعيد متاحة, يفتح مواعيد دفعة وحدة instead of التوفّر and التوليد الجماعي.

nodes.label: Concrete noun beats nominalisation
nodes.rationale: التوفّر and التوليد الجماعي are nominalisations the trainee must unpack before the sentence means anything; مواعيد متاحة needs no unpacking. The tell is a تفعّل/تفعيل-pattern noun where a plain one exists. Reported on Day-2 slide 12, 2026-09-25.

nodes.label: Terminology sweeps are semantic, never sed
nodes.rationale: Read every candidate in place. Incident: a blind swap on «صمّم محتوى الدورة ومنهجه» yields «صمّم منهج الدورة ومنهجه».

nodes.label: ايش is و+ايش: audit /وايش/
nodes.rationale: Write ايش unless a conjunction is genuinely needed (a list «مين هو، وايش دوره، ووين وصلتم» or two joined clauses). After an em-dash, a colon, or at the start of a title/clause there is nothing to join, so the و is wrong. Read every hit; the correct count is small.

nodes.label: Never label a task by who performs it
nodes.rationale: The trainee works on all 29 tasks; the source column «مَن ينفّذها» needed a footnote to stop it reading as 'I am not involved in nineteen of these', the tell it was wrong. Deck says «دورك فيها» and names a trainee action per row: تقرّر وتوصف (10), تراجع وتصحّح (7), تجرّب وتعدّل (12).

nodes.label: تكامل (the thing) vs ربط (the act)
nodes.rationale: Not synonyms; do not unify. تكامل is the subject of §7.5's title (an MCP connection), ربط is connecting one. Ordering rule: a slide before §7.5 must say ربط الأدوات الخارجية since التكاملات would be undefined to a cold reader.

nodes.label: Every task row opens with a verb
nodes.rationale: «المشكلة والهدف والغايات» is a label; «تحديد المشكلة والهدف والغايات» is a task. A vague row is rewritten to name its output: «بقيّة أصحاب المصلحة» became «تحديد الخدمات الخارجية والأطراف المتأثّرة بمشروعك».

nodes.label: Title states the takeaway, spoken Arabic
nodes.rationale: Compressed فصحى titles are a register failure: «حدّان يتجدّدان — لا رصيد لا نهائي» became «رصيدك يتجدّد لحاله، بس فيه حدّين لازم تعرفهم». A title must still describe the slide after it changes; two went stale unnoticed.

nodes.label: ؟ window belongs on the slide that uses the term
nodes.rationale: Incident: defining «كيان» on a Day-2 slide whose cards only said «الدور» was reported as actively confusing: the trainee hunts the slide for the word and doesn't find it. Grep the slide for the term before shipping a ؟; if absent move it and rewrite the sentence to introduce the idea.

nodes.label: Never use a term before its defining slide
nodes.rationale: «التكاملات» appeared 15 slides before §7.5 defined it; «متطلّب» belongs to §10 and must not leak into §8. If genuinely needed earlier, reorder rather than define twice.

nodes.label: No invented quantitative anchors
nodes.rationale: «45 رسالة قصيرة» was fabricated. If a number can't be sourced delete it and record why so it can't drift back. Prefer a measurable anchor (a 300-line file ≈ 4k tokens) over a rate.

nodes.label: Bidi: mechanical rules
nodes.rationale: Heading says 'four mechanical rules' but five bullets follow (the dimension-pair rule was added later).

nodes.label: End an Arabic sentence with an Arabic word
nodes.rationale: A sentence ending in a Latin word puts the full stop at the wrong end (`. read_email`).

nodes.label: Neutral char after isolated Latin jumps
nodes.rationale: A neutral character after an isolated Latin run jumps to the other end; reorder so the Latin token lands last in its clause.

nodes.label: Never chain A ← B inside one tok-lat
nodes.rationale: It reads left-to-right and reverses the order for an Arabic reader. Use two elements joined by an Arabic verb: «افتح Settings ثم اختر Usage». An arrow cannot fix this; a verb can.

nodes.label: LTR number box glues to Arabic in RTL cell
nodes.rationale: «8.1المشكلة» needs text-align: end and a min-width.

nodes.label: Dimension pair with × flips in Arabic text
nodes.rationale: «1200×630» between two Arabic runs renders backwards even with plain Latin digits; an isolating span does not reliably fix it. Say it in words: «عرضها 1200 وارتفاعها 630». Same for any A×B-shaped token.

nodes.label: Latin digits only, never ١٢٣
nodes.rationale: Mixed scripts read as inconsistent and Arabic-Indic digits reorder unpredictably beside Latin tokens in RTL. Audit /[٠-٩]/. Found on Day 1 and Day 2 stage__n badges and Day 3 EARS card ordinals as of 2026-09-29; fix on next touch, not proactively.

nodes.label: Never glue Arabic و to a Latin word
nodes.rationale: `وpush` / `وSupabase` render as one run and read as a typo. Use & when the و joins two Latin tokens that pair (commit & push), or a space (و Supabase) for an ordinary conjunction. Audit /و(?:<[^>]+>)*[A-Za-z]/ over the HTML and over rendered text, since the markup form misses cases that glue only after tags are stripped.

nodes.label: Four sessions per day
nodes.rationale: شرح المفاهيم, تطبيق مع المدرب, عملك على مشروعك, مراجعة وعرض التقدم.

nodes.label: Days 2-10 carry two session-break slides
nodes.rationale: From Day 2 the first two sessions are one interleaved block, so only «عملك على مشروعك» and «مراجعة وعرض التقدم» open with a break slide; the first doesn't either, since the day opens on شرح المفاهيم. Without breaks a trainee can't tell the session changed. Day 1 keeps three because its «تطبيق مع المدرب» is a separate device-setup walkthrough; do not 'fix' it down to two.

nodes.label: Break slide: full-bleed sag-quote frame
nodes.rationale: sag-slide sag-quote deck-slide, data-tone=rule, data-surface=dark; footer carries only the session badge (no logo, no day label). The only legitimate sag-quote use that is not a real pull-quote.

nodes.label: «ticking tasks is your job» attr line
nodes.rationale: The __attr line says what the session needs and nothing else covers; the عملك على مشروعك break tells the trainee that ticking finished tasks is their job.

nodes.label: Task rows: keys, nesting, cross-slide sync
nodes.rationale: .task rows are checkboxes (A.6.9). data-task-key = explicit id, data-parent = the key it rolls up into, task--l2/l3 = indentation. Markup stays a FLAT list; nesting .task elements would break the .tasks flex column and the .task grid.

nodes.label: Same data-task-key repaints everywhere
nodes.rationale: Day-plan slide lists «7.10 · تجهّز جهازك أنت» as one line while the work slide breaks it into eleven rows; ticking either moves both. Parent/child maps are built over keys, so a parent ticked on one slide cascades into children on another. A parent shows partial (dash) until a full house; clicking a partial parent fills it in.

nodes.label: Give syncing rows an explicit data-task-key
nodes.rationale: Matching on label text across slides is brittle: a ؟ qmark button's text is part of the label, so identical-looking rows aren't identical. Adding a key orphans whatever was stored under the old label-derived key; harmless between cohorts.

nodes.label: Look-alike rows can be different tasks
nodes.rationale: Day 1 has «7.10 · نستعرض خطوات تجهيز الجهاز أمامك» (trainer demos) and «7.10 · تجهّز جهازك أنت» (trainee does it): same section, two tasks, two keys, never merge.

nodes.label: Task rows assume a light surface
nodes.rationale: [data-done=true] paints a pale teal that white --text-heading would vanish into. Put the checklist on a light slide and let the break slide before it carry the dark.

nodes.label: Three surfaces must stay in sync
nodes.rationale: A wording change usually lives in more than one file; after any content edit grep all of them and report what you found.

nodes.label: project-package/slides/day-NN.html
nodes.rationale: The slides, including the <!-- ═══ N — title ═══ --> banner above each one.

nodes.label: bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.md
nodes.rationale: The authoring source. Headings own GitHub anchors, so renaming a heading breaks every link unless the TOC entry and every cross-reference move with it.

nodes.label: deck/ per-day briefs (DECK_BRIEF, day-NN-brief)
nodes.rationale: DECK_BRIEF.md is Day 1's (named before the convention existed), then day-02-brief.md and so on. All carry slide numbers that go stale when a slide is inserted.

nodes.label: deck/MEDIA_SHOTLIST.md
nodes.rationale: Covers every day, not just Day 1; after the 2026-09-25 showcase reversal days 2-10 got recordings of their own, each a section including shots not yet filmed (marked ⬜). deck/ holds only these planning docs.

nodes.label: The .docx curriculum mirror is retired
nodes.rationale: bootcamp_roadmap_and_curriculum.docx was a hand-edited Word mirror, painful to patch; trainees never read it. It sits in archive/ and is not maintained: do not edit it or re-add it to the sync list.

nodes.label: Footer numbers written by deck.js
nodes.rationale: Inserting a slide does not mean touching dozens of spans; the day label (.deck-foot__side .deck-foot__num) is hand-authored. DECK_BRIEF and MEDIA_SHOTLIST carry hand-written numbers: renumber bottom-up (top-down collides) and assert each row matches exactly once before replacing.

nodes.label: Verification checklist (report each result)
nodes.rationale: Run all and report each result rather than asserting success: deckAudit on the real page via chrome-devtools, screenshots, qmark grep, interactive behaviours, register sweeps, curriculum prompt count, term windows, commands as snipbox, break-slide count, checkbox hierarchy, anchors, offline.

nodes.label: Register sweep by verb family
nodes.rationale: Sweep يسو/تسو/نسو/سوّ, not one spelling. Incident: a clean single-spelling grep passed a «تسوي» written minutes earlier; the family sweep's first real run found three more on Day 1. Exclude the noun «المسوّدة»; read the rest in place.

nodes.label: .docx structure check item (stale?)
nodes.rationale: The checklist still lists '.docx structure: counts unchanged, TOC anchors resolve, jc=right = 0, 14 of 15 zip entries byte-identical' although the .docx is retired and not maintained.

nodes.label: Offline: no remote font/script/image
nodes.rationale: The training room may have no wifi, and a deck that loses its icons on stage is a failed deck.

nodes.label: Working method: gradual, few slides at a time
nodes.rationale: Fix THAT slide against everything above, leave the rest, then say which slides most need the same treatment next. The closing recommendation is part of the deliverable (A.6.10).

nodes.label: Reported defect is a sample, not the bug
nodes.rationale: Named one badly-styled slide, five more had the same fault; named three bad task rows, eleven were wrong. Fix the instance, enumerate the whole class, report both counts (how many checked, how many found).

nodes.label: Verification scope tracks edit scope
nodes.rationale: deckAudit and deckRefAudit are whole-deck and free, so always run them. Full text sweeps are for deck-wide changes only (terminology unification, new styling rule, deck.css edit). Opening every reply with a 50-slide verification after touching one slide was called out as waste.

nodes.label: New styling rule earns one deck-wide sweep
nodes.rationale: The rule is new, so nothing before it was built to comply. Then record what deliberately stays as-is so the next sweep does not re-flag it.

nodes.label: Redundant content is deleted, not reworded
nodes.rationale: When told something is already covered elsewhere, delete it rather than rescue it with a rewrite and a distinction. Then fix the grid's data-cols and hunt orphaned sentences that referenced it.

nodes.label: Bump banner numbers before inserting
nodes.rationale: Renumber every <!-- ═══ N — … --> at or above the insertion point first, then splice the new slide in with its own banner; the other way round catches the new banner in the same pass. Back up before the splice; deletions are the mirror operation.

nodes.label: Validate the validator
nodes.rationale: Before trusting a custom audit script, prove it fails on deliberately broken input. Incident: one reported 55 phantom broken links because its slug rules didn't match GitHub's; the real count was zero.

nodes.label: ffmpeg exit code 0 is not success
nodes.rationale: Verify by duration, frame count or pixel comparison. A mangled path once produced a silently truncated file at exit 0, and a bad flag produced two empty frames that compared as 'identical'.

nodes.label: 'Leave it alone' decisions are scoped
nodes.rationale: The handout was deliberately left stale for three days because reconciling it sat outside that session's scope; a later session explicitly asked to reconcile it and did. That is a new in-scope decision superseding an old out-of-scope one, not a reversal. Read an old note for the scope it was made under.

nodes.label: Reversed rule needs its trigger restated
nodes.rationale: 'Every screen needs an origin' kept its wording across a reshape but flipped meaning: once Claude extracts first, it is dead weight unless re-scoped to screens the trainee adds. The same mistake shipped again one turn later inside the fix. Ask what has actually happened by this step, not whether it matches what you already know to avoid.

nodes.label: Reviewing AI output is not stating what only the trainee knows
nodes.rationale: A review-structure reshape (passes, gap list, origin field) can improve a task while staying entirely about checking Claude's work; nothing asks the trainee to say what was never in the source data. When a task's purpose is 'trainee input matters', check for an actual elicitation prompt, not a count of review steps.

nodes.label: A list for later is not acting on it now
nodes.rationale: A correct gap list (steps/requirements with no matching screen) still hands the resolution work back to the trainee if it is displayed and left. The fix is not a better list but asking about each item immediately, in the same turn.

nodes.label: Existing affordance under a different name
nodes.rationale: Asked for 'an icon that explains RTL and LTR', the real need (click a marker, see a definition) was already .qmark + <template class=terms>. Check existing components before adding a new one.

nodes.label: Report honestly
nodes.rationale: If a measurement contradicts something you said earlier, say so plainly and move on.
